reasoning_traces.think:
The Restricted Betting Theorem establishes that when return distributions are unbounded, the theoretical Kelly optimal bet fraction K* collapses to zero, regardless of mean-to-standard-deviation ratio. This occurs because the support function constraint h_X(-K) ≤ 1 becomes infeasible for unbounded sets, forcing K* = 0. In contrast, empirical Kelly uses a non-parametric estimate of the distribution, f̂_X(x), which avoids the assumption of unbounded support. As such, it can yield positive, meaningful stakes even when theoretical Kelly fails. The core duality lies in the distinction between parametric modeling (where model class determines outcome) and empirical estimation (which adapts to observed data). The failure mode manifests in GSE when it applies a normal distribution fit to returns, which inherently assumes unbounded support. The remedy is to compute stakes directly from the empirical distribution of engine-generated edges, bypassing parametric assumptions. This aligns with the principle that bounded support is necessary for non-degenerate Kelly betting. The support function constraint h_X(-K) ≤ 1 defines the boundary of feasible bets, and its violation under unbounded support leads to infeasibility. Thus, the theorem reveals a critical design flaw in GSE’s probabilistic reasoning pipeline when it assumes unboundedness in return models.
